title: Uncapped Indemnification Liability
ruleText: Uncapped indemnification obligations, indemnification extending to consequential, indirect, or punitive damages, or absence of mutual liability limitations.
example: Supplier shall indemnify and hold Customer harmless against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, and losses whatsoever without monetary limitation.

title: Sole Negligence & Gross Negligence Indemnity
ruleText: Indemnification clauses requiring a party to indemnify the other against the indemnified party's own negligence, willful misconduct, or strict liability.
example: Customer agrees to indemnify Provider against all liabilities arising from the performance of Services, including Provider's own ordinary or gross negligence.

title: Non-Reciprocal Third-Party IP Defense
ruleText: Indemnification obligations or warranty disclaimers lacking reciprocal IP infringement defense, or placing unilateral defense costs on recipient.
example: Vendor disclaims all warranties of non-infringement and Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor for any claims arising out of Customer data.

title: Broad Environmental or Regulatory Indemnification
ruleText: Uncapped or strict indemnification covering past environmental compliance, regulatory fines, or government investigations beyond fault.
example: Contractor indemnifies Company for any environmental sanctions or governmental penalties regardless of causation or timing.

title: Indemnification for Indirect/Consequential Damages
ruleText: Indemnification scope explicitly covering lost profits, diminution of goodwill, or punitive damages.
example: Party A shall indemnify Party B for any loss of business, prospective profits, or indirect damages resulting from breach.

title: Complete Waiver of Limitation of Liability
ruleText: Complete absence or express exclusion of an aggregate liability cap for general contract breach or performance failures.
example: Neither party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall be subject to any monetary cap or threshold.

title: One-Way Unlimited Liability
ruleText: Asymmetric aggregate cap where one party's liability is capped at a minor amount while the other party faces unlimited liability.
example: Customer's liability is limited to fees paid in previous 1 month, whereas Provider's liability shall be uncapped.

title: Uncapped Liquidated Damages
ruleText: Liquidated damages provisions without aggregate caps or daily limits, functioning effectively as punitive penalties.
example: Contractor pays $10,000 per day of delay without cap until project delivery is accepted by Client.

title: Exclusion of Consequential Damages Carve-Out Violation
ruleText: Unilateral carve-outs allowing one party to claim indirect or lost profits while prohibiting the counterparty.
example: Client shall not be liable for indirect damages, but Vendor remains liable for Client's lost profits and reputation damage.

title: Disproportionate Liability Cap Multiplier
ruleText: Liability cap set at an exorbitant multiple (e.g., 10x to 50x annual contract value) detached from commercial fee realities.
example: Provider's total liability shall not exceed 25 times the total fees paid under this Agreement.

title: Immediate Unilateral Termination Without Cause
ruleText: Right of one party to terminate immediately without cause, notice period, or obligation to pay accrued fees or work-in-progress.
example: Company may terminate this agreement at any time with immediate effect upon oral notification without compensation.

title: Immediate Termination on Mere Allegation
ruleText: Termination for material breach without a mandatory cure period (e.g., 0 days cure) based on mere unsubstantiated claims.
example: Customer may terminate for default immediately without giving Vendor opportunity to cure any alleged deficiency.

title: Perpetual Lock-In and Non-Cancellable Long-Term Commitment
ruleText: Multi-year agreements with no early termination right, onerous acceleration of remaining term fees upon any termination.
example: In the event of termination by Client for any reason, all fees through the 5-year term immediately become due and payable.

title: Post-Termination Forfeiture of Pre-Paid Balances
ruleText: Clauses declaring that upon termination without cause by vendor, client forfeits all unearned pre-paid subscriptions.
example: All fees paid in advance are non-refundable under all circumstances, even upon Vendor's termination for convenience.

title: Perpetual Confidentiality for Operational Boilerplate
ruleText: Perpetual confidentiality obligations on standard business or technical information lacking trade secret qualifications.
example: Recipient shall maintain all disclosed information confidential in perpetuity without time limitation.

title: No Exclusion for Legally Compelled Disclosure
ruleText: Confidentiality clauses omitting standard exclusions for disclosures required by court order, subpoena, or securities regulators.
example: Recipient may not disclose Confidential Information under any circumstances, even if mandated by judicial decree.

title: Strict Strict-Liability Trade Secret Warranties
ruleText: Imposing strict liability or criminal standard compliance on data breach without requiring proof of fault or reasonable security measures.
example: Any unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information shall constitute an irremediable breach subject to liquidated damages of $1M.

title: Forfeiture of Pre-Existing Background IP
ruleText: Assigning all right, title, and interest in pre-existing background IP or generic tools/frameworks to the counterparty.
example: All intellectual property developed, utilized, or incorporated by Consultant shall become the sole property of Client.

title: Broad Work Made For Hire on Vendor Software Core
ruleText: Work made for hire provisions granting customer exclusive ownership over vendor's foundational algorithms and reusable code.
example: All deliverables and underlying software engines are works made for hire and Client owns all copyright and patents.

title: Perpetual Exclusive License Without Royalty
ruleText: Granting an irrevocable, perpetual, exclusive worldwide license with no ongoing royalty, minimum purchase, or right of revocation.
example: Licensor grants Licensee an exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up license to commercialize Licensor's technology.

title: No IP Non-Infringement Warranty by Provider
ruleText: Software or IP licensing agreements where the licensor completely disclaims ownership and freedom-to-operate warranties.
example: Software is provided AS IS with zero warranty against third party patent, trademark or copyright infringement.

title: Waiver of Jury Trial and Class Action Prohibition
ruleText: One-sided waivers stripping parties of statutory defense rights, class representation, or injunctive relief.
example: Party B unconditionally waives any right to jury trial or injunctive defense in any court of competent jurisdiction.

title: Foreign Jurisdiction and Non-Neutral Governing Law
ruleText: Mandatory dispute resolution in a foreign, high-risk jurisdiction with no connection to the contracting parties.
example: This agreement shall be governed solely by the laws of offshore Cayman Islands and litigated exclusively in Grand Cayman.

title: Unilateral Right to Amend Contract Terms
ruleText: Permitting one party to unilaterally modify contract terms, pricing, or service scope upon web posting without counterparty consent.
example: Service Provider reserves the right to modify these terms, prices, and SLAs at any time without prior written notice.

title: Blanket Unrestricted Audit Rights
ruleText: Allowing full physical and digital inspection of all facilities, source code, and employee records with zero notice.
example: Buyer may inspect and audit Supplier's entire corporate facilities, books, and code repositories at any hour without notice.

title: Indemnification for Data Breaches Beyond Causation
ruleText: Demanding full indemnity for corporate-wide security breaches regardless of whether supplier followed industry security standards.
example: Vendor indemnifies Client for all data breach liabilities regardless of whether the breach occurred in Vendor's environment.

title: Unlimited Consequential Liability for Software Bugs
ruleText: Failure to disclaim lost business profits for standard software outages or bugs.
example: Developer shall be liable for all lost business revenues resulting from downtime or defective code releases.

title: Post-Termination Non-Compete and Market Restrictions
ruleText: Broad non-compete covenants preventing a vendor from servicing other clients in the industry for multiple years.
example: Provider shall not offer software services to any entity in the financial services sector for 3 years post-termination.

title: Compulsory Source Code Escrow Release on Minor Breach
ruleText: Escrow release triggered by minor operational dispute rather than bankruptcy or cessation of business operations.
example: Deposit agent shall immediately release all proprietary source code to Client upon written claim of SLA breach.

title: Full Indemnity for Tax Liabilities of Counterparty
ruleText: Shifting the counterparty's corporate, income, or payroll tax obligations onto the service provider.
example: Contractor agrees to indemnify Client against any and all corporate income, payroll, and value added taxes levied on Client.

title: Open-Ended Defense Cost Undertaking
ruleText: Obligation to pay counterparty's attorney fees immediately upon receipt of third-party notice before liability adjudication.
example: Indemnitor shall pay Indemnitee's legal defense invoices within 10 days of presentation regardless of final outcome.

title: No Liability Cap on Data Protection Claims
ruleText: Excluding data security and privacy claims entirely from the aggregate liability limitation without sub-caps.
example: The limitation of liability in Section 8 shall not apply to any claims involving data security, privacy, or GDPR.

title: Automatic Renewal with Draconian Opt-Out Window
ruleText: Auto-renewing for multi-year terms unless notice is delivered in an unreasonably narrow window (e.g. exactly 5 days before renewal).
example: Agreement renews for 3-year successive terms unless notice is received between day 90 and day 85 prior to expiration.

title: Liquidated Damages for Inadvertent Confidentiality Spill
ruleText: Pre-stipulated steep penalties for any non-intentional confidentiality breach without showing demonstrable harm.
example: Any inadvertent breach of Section 6 incurs immediate liquidated damages of $250,000 per occurrence.

title: Assignment of Customer Feedback into Exclusive Rights
ruleText: Clauses where customer suggestions grant vendor total ownership over customer proprietary product roadmap.
example: Customer assigns all patent and commercial rights in any ideas, feedback, or joint workshop suggestions to Vendor.

title: Cross-Default with Unrelated Contracts
ruleText: Breach of any separate agreement between affiliates triggers immediate default and acceleration under this agreement.
example: A default under any contract between Supplier affiliates and Customer affiliates shall constitute an immediate event of default.

title: Indemnification Extending to Patent Claims Without Injunction Defense
ruleText: Indemnitor forced to defend worldwide patent infringement claims without having sole control of defense strategy.
example: Indemnitor shall defend patent claims but Indemnitee reserves right to settle without Indemnitor's approval.

title: Unlimited Warranty Liability for Third-Party Components
ruleText: Holding service provider strictly liable for open source or third-party cloud infrastructure failures.
example: Supplier guarantees 100% uptime of third-party cloud infrastructure and assumes unlimited liability for outages.

title: Termination upon Change of Control Triggering Penalty
ruleText: Triggering steep penalty fees if a company undergoes merger, recapitalization, or acquisition.
example: If Vendor undergoes change of control, Client may terminate and Vendor shall pay 12 months fees as liquidation fee.

title: Strict Criminal Background Disclosures of Personnel
ruleText: Requiring disclosure of employee personal medical, biometric, or private records violating local privacy statutes.
example: Contractor must disclose full biometric and medical screening records of all staff assigned to account.

title: Mandatory Patent Cross-License Grant-Back
ruleText: Requiring licensee to grant back royalty-free worldwide patent rights for any improvement made during term.
example: Licensee grants Licensor a perpetual, royalty-free, exclusive license to any improvements invented by Licensee.

title: Exclusive Dealing and Restraint of Trade
ruleText: Prohibiting a party from engaging in ordinary commercial transactions with competitors across all lines of business.
example: Supplier shall not provide any IT consulting services to any other enterprise in North America.

title: Waiving All Defenses to Consequential Damages
ruleText: Explicit clause declaring that all lost revenues and customer goodwill shall be deemed direct damages.
example: The parties agree that lost revenue, goodwill, and business opportunity shall be treated as direct damages hereunder.

title: Uncapped Environmental Contamination Indemnity
ruleText: Requiring indemnification for pre-existing environmental hazards unknown at contract execution.
example: Lessee agrees to indemnify Lessor for all environmental contamination discovered on premises regardless of date of origin.

title: Unilateral Sanctions Acceleration
ruleText: Permitting immediate contract forfeiture and asset freezing based on unilateral determination of compliance concern.
example: Client may unilaterally freeze all payments and seize equipment upon its sole suspicion of regulatory concern.

title: Asymmetric Indemnification Obligations
ruleText: One party provides comprehensive indemnity while the other party provides no reciprocal indemnity for IP or breach.
example: Provider indemnifies Customer against breach, but Customer provides no indemnification for misuse of deliverables.

title: Short Notice Requirement for Indemnity Defense
ruleText: Strict requirement to tender defense within unrealistically short period (e.g., 48 hours) or forfeit indemnification.
example: Indemnitee must give written notice within 2 business days of claim notice or waive all indemnification rights.

title: Indemnification for Indirect Regulatory Penalties
ruleText: Indemnification covering administrative agency inquiries without a finding of fault.
example: Contractor shall reimburse Customer for expenses incurred responding to regulatory inquiries regarding Contractor's work.

title: Asymmetric Liability Cap Multipliers
ruleText: Liability cap set at 2x to 3x annual fees, or differing liability caps between Customer and Supplier.
example: Provider's liability is capped at 3x annual contract value, whereas Customer's liability is capped at 1x contract value.

title: High Multiple Super-Caps for Data Security
ruleText: Data protection liability super-cap set at 5x annual fees rather than standard insurance-backed coverage.
example: Liability for data privacy breaches shall be subject to a special super-cap equal to 5 times annual contract value.

title: Liquidated Damages as Sole Remedy Without Disclaimers
ruleText: Liquidated damages provisions that lack clarity on whether they constitute sole and exclusive remedy.
example: Delay penalties shall accrue at $1,000/day; Client reserves right to pursue further breach damages concurrently.

title: Short Cure Period for Material Breach
ruleText: Cure period for material breach set under 15 days (e.g., 5 to 10 days) for complex technical or operational covenants.
example: Either party may terminate for material breach if the breach is not remedied within 7 calendar days of notice.

title: Unilateral Attorney Fee Shifting in Litigation
ruleText: Unilateral attorney fee shifting in litigation or unilateral audit rights lacking at least 15 business days' prior written notice.
example: If Customer prevails in any action under this Agreement, Vendor shall pay Customer's full attorney fees.

title: Termination for Convenience with Inadequate Notice
ruleText: Termination for convenience permitted on 15 to 29 days' notice without structured off-boarding or transition assistance.
example: Customer may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice to Provider.

title: Termination Triggered by Insolvency or Material Adverse Change
ruleText: Allowing termination on subjective material adverse financial change before formal bankruptcy proceedings.
example: Either party may terminate if in its reasonable judgment the other party's creditworthiness has materially deteriorated.

title: Overly Broad Definition of Confidential Information
ruleText: Defining all communications, whether marked or unmarked, as confidential without standard marking requirements.
example: Confidential Information shall include all oral statements and written materials exchanged between the parties.

title: Extended Confidentiality Duration Beyond Standard Term
ruleText: Confidentiality duration of 5 to 10 years for ordinary commercial data.
example: The obligations of non-disclosure shall survive termination of this Agreement for a period of 7 years.

title: Mandatory Return or Destruction Without Archival Exception
ruleText: Obligation to destroy all confidential data without carve-outs for automated backup tapes and statutory record retention.
example: Within 5 days of termination, Recipient must purge all Confidential Information from every server and certify destruction.

title: Ambiguous Work Product Assignment Scope
ruleText: Vague language regarding whether newly created custom configurations or integrations transfer to client.
example: All developments and work product generated in connection with the project shall belong to Client.

title: Non-Exclusive License with Narrow Sublicensing Rights
ruleText: Granting client right to sublicense vendor technology to arbitrary third parties without vendor prior approval.
example: Customer receives a perpetual, non-exclusive license with full right to sublicense to affiliated commercial entities.

title: Restrictive Trademark and Publicity Covenants
ruleText: Prohibiting vendor from listing client's name or logo in customer lists without unreasonable approval hurdles.
example: Neither party shall disclose the existence of this relationship or use counterparty logo without executive sign-off.

title: Unfavorable Dispute Resolution Forum
ruleText: Mandating litigation in a remote domestic state rather than neutral jurisdiction or mutual home courts.
example: Any legal action shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware.

title: Mandatory Binding Arbitration with High Fee Sharing
ruleText: Imposing AAA or ICC arbitration with no streamlined procedure for claims under $100,000.
example: All disputes shall be resolved by three arbitrators under ICC rules in New York City with costs shared equally.

title: Non-Solicitation Restrictions of Personnel
ruleText: Broad non-solicitation covenants covering general job advertisements or unassigned employees.
example: Neither party shall hire or solicit any employee of the other party during the term and for 12 months thereafter.

title: Annual Price Escalation Index Linked to Uncapped Inflation
ruleText: Permitting automatic annual fee increases tied to inflation indices without a ceiling percentage cap.
example: Subscription fees shall increase annually on the anniversary date by the percentage increase in CPI plus 3%.

title: Audit Frequency Exceeding Once Per Calendar Year
ruleText: Audit clauses allowing multiple inspections per year or audits by direct market competitors.
example: Buyer may conduct up to three audits per calendar year of Seller's operational processes.

title: Conditioned Indemnity on Strict Defense Cooperation
ruleText: Allowing indemnitor to disclaim liability if indemnified party fails to provide minor administrative assistance.
example: Failure to provide requested case files within 5 days releases Indemnitor from all defense obligations.

title: Exclusion of Gross Negligence from Liability Cap
ruleText: Standard exclusion of gross negligence where gross negligence is loosely defined under foreign law standards.
example: The limitation of liability shall not apply to damages caused by gross negligence or reckless conduct.

title: Transition Services Without Rate Agreement
ruleText: Requiring provider to offer post-termination transition services for up to 6 months at unspecified legacy rates.
example: Vendor must provide transition assistance for up to 180 days upon termination at current contractual rates.

title: Residual Knowledge Exception Ambiguity
ruleText: Residual knowledge clause allowing counterparty employees to use retained mental impressions without safeguard.
example: Either party may use information retained in unaided human memory for any commercial purpose.

title: Invention Assignment of Off-Hours Developments
ruleText: Invention assignment clauses claiming developments created by contractor without client tools or client time.
example: Contractor assigns all inventions conceived during the term of engagement relating to Client's general industry.

title: Payment Terms Exceeding 60 Days
ruleText: Net payment terms extending past 60 or 90 days without interest on overdue balances.
example: Invoices shall be payable Net 75 days from date of receipt by Customer accounting department.

title: Right of Set-Off Against Future Invoices
ruleText: Allowing customer to withhold payments on current invoices due to disputed claims under separate statements of work.
example: Customer may set off any amounts owed by Vendor against any invoice payable under this Agreement.

title: Strict Compliance with Customer Internal Policies Without Copy
ruleText: Requiring vendor adherence to customer internal policies without attaching or providing copies of policies.
example: Vendor shall adhere to all Customer codes of conduct and security standards as amended from time to time.

title: Service Level Credits as Non-Exclusive Remedy
ruleText: Service level credits do not explicitly constitute the exclusive financial remedy for SLA downtime.
example: SLA uptime credits shall be issued monthly; Customer retains all common law damages remedies for downtime.

title: Indemnification for Pre-Existing Intellectual Property Inaccuracies
ruleText: Indemnity covering third party components without clear territorial bounds (worldwide vs specific countries).
example: Supplier indemnifies Customer against IP infringement claims brought in any jurisdiction worldwide.

title: Unilateral Extension of Contract Term
ruleText: Allowing one party to unilaterally extend contract term by option notice without renegotiation.
example: Customer reserves the unilateral option to extend this agreement for two additional one-year periods.

title: Personal Identifiable Information Handling Without DPA
ruleText: Contract transfers PII or personal data without an executed formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
example: Vendor shall process customer employee user data as necessary to perform the services hereunder.

title: Patent Defense Restrictions on Settlement
ruleText: Preventing indemnitor from settling a claim by substituting equivalent non-infringing software.
example: Settlement of any IP claim requires prior written approval of Customer, even if involving no financial admission.

title: Unilateral Right to Change Service Specifications
ruleText: Client right to order changes in deliverable scope without formal bilateral Change Order procedure.
example: Client may adjust deliverable milestones and scope by providing written specifications to Project Lead.

title: Warranty Period Exceeding 12 Months
ruleText: Custom software warranty period extending for 2 to 3 years post-acceptance.
example: Developer warrants software against material defects for a period of 24 months following final acceptance.

title: Aggregate Cap Calculated on Trailing 3 Months Only
ruleText: Limiting customer recovery to an excessively small fraction of the contract value (e.g. trailing 3 months fees).
example: Vendor's maximum liability is limited to fees paid during the three (3) months preceding the incident.

title: Indemnification Arising from Customer Modifications
ruleText: Indemnity that does not clearly carve out claims resulting from modifications made by the customer.
example: Provider indemnifies against patent infringement, unless modified by Customer in an unauthorized manner.

title: Immediate Termination for Reputational Harm
ruleText: Subjective termination right if one party's brand is perceived to be negatively impacted by counterparty news.
example: Either party may terminate if the other party is subject to negative publicity or public scandal.

title: Mandatory Notification of Security Inquiries Within 12 Hours
ruleText: Unrealistically tight incident notification window for minor inquiries not involving actual data breach.
example: Vendor must notify Customer within 12 hours of receiving any inquiry from information security regulators.

title: Joint IP Ownership Without Defined Exploitation Rights
ruleText: Declaring joint ownership of newly developed IP without establishing royalty and licensing rights between co-owners.
example: Any intellectual property developed jointly shall be owned jointly by the parties.

title: Severability Clause Without Reform Covenant
ruleText: Severability provision where invalid terms are stricken without requiring court to reform terms to mirror intent.
example: If any provision is held unenforceable, such provision shall be severed and remainder shall remain in effect.

title: Time is of the Essence Clause on Ancillary Obligations
ruleText: Declaring time is of the essence for administrative reporting rather than core product delivery dates.
example: Time is of the essence with respect to all quarterly performance report delivery dates.

title: No Exclusion of Force Majeure for Critical Obligations
ruleText: Force majeure clause omitting standard excused performance for natural disasters or cloud provider blackouts.
example: Failure of telecommunications or electric utilities shall not excuse performance under Section 4.

title: Termination upon Failure of Minority Milestone
ruleText: Permitting total contract termination for a 2-day delay on a non-critical interim design draft.
example: Client may terminate the entire Agreement for default if Interim Milestone 2 is delayed by more than 48 hours.

title: Recipient Bears Full Burden of Proof on Exceptions
ruleText: Shifting entire evidentiary burden onto recipient to establish that public information was lawfully obtained.
example: Recipient must produce written contemporaneous records to establish applicability of confidentiality exceptions.

title: Customer Retains Broad Derivative Work Rights on Deliverables
ruleText: Granting customer rights to create derivative works that may compete with vendor core product lines.
example: Customer may modify, decompile, and create derivative works of deliverables for internal operations.

title: Mandatory Insurance Minimums Beyond Standard Commercial Practice
ruleText: Requiring cyber or errors & omissions insurance policy limits disproportionate to contract size (e.g. $10M for a $50k deal).
example: Vendor must maintain $10,000,000 in Cyber Errors and Omissions insurance throughout the term.

title: Indemnification for Third Party Open Source License Compliance
ruleText: Requiring supplier to indemnify customer for any non-compliance with copyleft licenses in third party libraries.
example: Supplier indemnifies Customer against all claims alleging GPL or copyleft license violations in third party libraries.

title: Non-Assignment Without Consent Even to Affiliates
ruleText: Prohibiting corporate restructuring, merger, or affiliate assignment without counterparty's prior written consent.
example: Neither party may assign this agreement, including to an affiliate or successor in interest, without consent.

title: Standard Mutual IP Indemnification
ruleText: Mutual indemnification for third-party copyright, patent, and trade secret claims, conditioned on prompt notice and defense control.
example: Each party shall defend and indemnify the other against third-party claims alleging that its respective technology infringes IP rights.

title: Express Defense Control and Settlement Approval
ruleText: Indemnitor has sole control of defense with proviso that settlements requiring financial contribution need indemnitee consent.
example: Indemnitor shall control defense; neither party shall settle any claim admitting liability without the other's prior written consent.

title: Prompt Notice Requirement for Indemnity
ruleText: Prompt written notice required within 30 days of receiving claim, with forfeiture only if failure prejudices defense.
example: Indemnitee shall provide prompt written notice of claims; failure to give prompt notice releases liability only to extent prejudiced.

title: Standard 1x Annual Contract Value Liability Cap
ruleText: Mutual aggregate liability cap equal to total fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the incident.
example: Each party's total aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid in the preceding twelve (12) months.

title: Mutual Exclusion of Consequential and Indirect Damages
ruleText: Bilateral disclaimer of indirect, special, incidental, punitive, or consequential damages.
example: Neither party shall be liable for any indirect, special, incidental, or consequential damages, including loss of profits.

title: Reasonable Liquidated Damages as Exclusive Remedy
ruleText: Clearly stipulated reasonable delay credits capped at 10% of statement of work as sole financial remedy.
example: SLA uptime credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for unavailability of the hosted service.

title: Standard 30-Day Cure Period for Material Breach
ruleText: Either party may terminate for material breach upon 30 days' advance written notice with opportunity to cure.
example: Either party may terminate upon written notice if the other party fails to cure a material breach within thirty (30) days.

title: Mutual Termination for Convenience with 30+ Days Notice
ruleText: Mutual right to terminate for convenience upon at least 30 to 60 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of unearned fees.
example: Mutual termination for convenience permitted upon at least 30 days' advance written notice with pro-rata refund of unearned fees.

title: Termination upon Formal Involuntary Bankruptcy
ruleText: Termination permitted if the other party files bankruptcy, enters liquidation, or ceases commercial operations.
example: Either party may terminate if the other party dissolves, files for bankruptcy, or has a receiver appointed.

title: Standard 3-Year Confidentiality Term with Trade Secret Carve-Out
ruleText: Confidentiality duration of 3 to 5 years, preserving indefinite protection solely for legitimate trade secrets.
example: Confidentiality obligations shall continue for three (3) years post-termination, except trade secrets shall remain protected indefinitely.

title: Standard Commercial Confidentiality Exclusions
ruleText: Express exclusions for public information, already known data, independently developed materials, and court-compelled disclosures.
example: Confidential Information does not include data already public, known prior to disclosure, independently developed, or court-mandated.

title: Standard Legal Process Notice and Protective Order
ruleText: Obligation to give prompt notice of subpoena or court order so disclosing party can seek a protective order.
example: If legally compelled to disclose, recipient shall provide prompt notice to enable disclosing party to seek protective orders.

title: Reservation of Pre-Existing Background Intellectual Property
ruleText: Each party retains all right, title, and interest in its pre-existing background IP and foundational tools.
example: Each party retains exclusive ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property, proprietary tools, and standard software.

title: Non-Exclusive Customer License to Deliverables
ruleText: Customer receives a perpetual, non-exclusive, internal business-use license for completed custom deliverables.
example: Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use the deliverables for its internal business operations.

title: Express Feedback License Without Mandatory Assignment
ruleText: Feedback granted as non-exclusive, royalty-free license without forcing customer to assign future product rights.
example: Customer grants Vendor a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback for product improvements.

title: Neutral Governing Law and Venue
ruleText: Standard neutral corporate jurisdiction (e.g., New York, Delaware, or California) with reciprocal court access.
example: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law principles.

title: Standard Bilateral Dispute Escalation and Mediation
ruleText: Executive negotiation followed by commercial mediation before initiating formal court proceedings.
example: Disputes shall first be referred to executive officers for 30 days, followed by non-binding mediation prior to litigation.

title: Permitted Assignment to Affiliates or Merger Successors
ruleText: Either party may assign agreement without consent in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of substantially all assets.
example: Either party may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or successor in interest in connection with a merger or acquisition.

title: Standard Force Majeure with Written Notice
ruleText: Excusing performance during unforeseeable natural catastrophes, wars, or governmental shutdowns with duty to mitigate.
example: Neither party shall be liable for delay resulting from acts of God, strikes, pandemics, or government orders.

title: Standard Net 30 Day Payment Terms
ruleText: Standard commercial payment terms of Net 30 days from date of valid invoice receipt.
example: Customer shall pay undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days from receipt.

title: Standard Severability and Reformation
ruleText: Court may reform unenforceable provisions to effect original intent, preserving valid clauses.
example: If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall continue in effect and the invalid clause reformed to reflect parties' intent.

title: Entire Agreement and Written Amendments
ruleText: Standard integration clause requiring written amendments signed by authorized representatives.
example: This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding and may only be amended in writing signed by authorized representatives.

title: Standard Notices via Electronic Mail and Certified Post
ruleText: Notices effective upon confirmed email transmission or recognized commercial courier delivery.
example: All formal notices must be in writing and delivered via email with confirmed receipt or overnight courier.

title: Independent Contractor Status
ruleText: Explicit confirmation of independent contractor relationship with no joint venture, agency, or partnership.
example: The parties are independent contractors; nothing herein shall create an agency, partnership, or employment relationship.

title: Customer Indemnity for Customer-Supplied Data
ruleText: Customer indemnifies vendor for claims alleging customer-provided data infringes privacy or third-party IP rights.
example: Customer agrees to defend Vendor against claims alleging that Customer data violates third-party copyright or privacy.

title: Mutual Symmetrical Aggregate Liability Cap
ruleText: Equal liability caps applied evenly to both parties without asymmetric advantage.
example: Each party's aggregate liability shall be limited to amounts paid or payable under the applicable Statement of Work.

title: Orderly Data Return and Transition on Expiry
ruleText: Structured protocol for export of customer data in standard format upon termination at no extra charge.
example: Upon expiration, Vendor shall make Customer data available for download in CSV/JSON format for forty-five (45) days.

title: Reasonable Security Standard for Confidential Data
ruleText: Standard duty of care equal to the degree of care used for own confidential data, not less than reasonable care.
example: Each party shall protect confidential information with the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential data.

title: Standard Non-Infringement Warranty with Replacement Remedy
ruleText: Warranty of non-infringement with standard remedy: procure right to use, replace with equivalent, or refund pro-rata.
example: If software is held to infringe, Licensor shall procure the right to continue use, replace with non-infringing software, or refund.

title: Reasonable Annual Audit with 15 Business Days Notice
ruleText: Annual audit during normal business hours upon at least 15 business days' notice at auditor's expense.
example: Audits shall occur during normal business hours upon 15 business days' written notice not more than once per year.

title: Mutual Non-Disparagement During Term
ruleText: Mutual commitment not to make false or defamatory public statements concerning counterparty.
example: Neither party shall publish defamatory, derogatory, or disparaging statements regarding the other party.

title: Insurance Carve-In to Liability Caps
ruleText: Explicit provision that insurance policy proceeds shall be credited toward liability settlements.
example: Amounts recovered from third-party insurance policies shall be credited toward applicable liability limits.

title: Survival of Accrued Rights and Payment Obligations
ruleText: Termination does not waive accrued payment obligations or liability for prior breaches.
example: Termination shall not affect rights or obligations accrued prior to effective date of termination.

title: Standard Residual Memory Knowledge Carve-Out
ruleText: Permitting use of non-specific general ideas retained in unaided human memory without copying documentation.
example: General skills and techniques retained in unaided memory without deliberate memorization may be used.

title: Vendor Owns Platform Metrics and De-Identified Telemetry
ruleText: Vendor retains right to aggregate, anonymize, and analyze telemetry to improve infrastructure security and uptime.
example: Vendor may aggregate de-identified system telemetry to monitor performance and improve the service.

title: Good Faith Dispute Resolution Period
ruleText: Mandatory 20-day informal discussion period before issuing formal legal notices of default.
example: Parties agree to attempt good-faith informal resolution for twenty (20) days prior to issuing breach notice.

title: Indemnification Cap Aligned with Comprehensive Insurance
ruleText: Liability indemnification backed by standard commercial general liability and errors & omissions insurance.
example: Indemnity obligations for property damage shall be backed by commercial general liability policy limits.

title: Mutual Limitation for Open Source Software
ruleText: Standard disclaimer of warranties for third-party open source components included under MIT/Apache licenses.
example: Third-party open-source libraries are governed by their respective licenses without supplemental warranties.

title: Pro-Rata Refund of Prepaid Fees upon Breach by Vendor
ruleText: Customer receives pro-rata refund of prepaid unearned fees if customer terminates for vendor uncured breach.
example: If Customer terminates for Vendor breach, Vendor shall refund prepaid fees for the remaining unused term.

title: Safe Harbor for Standard Auditor Disclosures
ruleText: Confidentiality disclosure permitted to legal counsel, accountants, and insurers bound by professional ethics.
example: Disclosures are permitted to financial and legal advisors under confidentiality duties comparable to this Agreement.

title: Customer Retains Full Ownership of Customer Data
ruleText: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in all data uploaded or processed through the platform.
example: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data, and Vendor acquires no ownership rights therein.

title: Waiver Must Be Explicit and In Writing
ruleText: Failure to enforce any covenant does not constitute an ongoing or future waiver of that right.
example: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party granting the waiver.

title: Counterparts and Electronic Signatures Valid
ruleText: Contract may be executed in counterparts and via electronic signature tools (DocuSign/AdobeSign).
example: This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and electronically, each of which shall be deemed an original.

title: Standard Currency and Tax Apportionment
ruleText: Prices quoted in USD with customer responsible for sales/use taxes and vendor responsible for income taxes.
example: All fees are payable in USD and exclusive of applicable sales taxes, which shall be invoiced to Customer.

title: Termination upon Failure of Key Condition Precedent
ruleText: Contract permits termination without penalty if mandatory governmental license or regulatory approval is denied.
example: Either party may terminate without penalty if required regulatory export authorizations are denied.

title: Direct Damages Cap with Standard Multiplier
ruleText: Direct damages cap standard 12-month fees with clear definition of recoverable direct damage types.
example: Direct damages recoverable by either party shall be capped at the fees paid in the preceding 12 months.

title: Heading Section Captions For Convenience Only
ruleText: Clause headings and titles are inserted for convenience only and do not affect legal interpretation.
example: Section headings are for reference purposes only and shall not limit or interpret the text of any provision.
